doom.driver: Oil shipments are under attack on multiple fronts as fighting escalates in Red Sea, Hormuz and Black Sea. More than 60 commercial ships have been attacked in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman since March 1.
doom.blurb: SIXTY SHIPS DOWN. THREE STRAITS. ONE VERY BAD MONTH.
doom.summary: While Pakistan floats peace talks and oil dips 3%, the score on the board reads: 60+ commercial vessels attacked across three of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints since March. Saudi Arabia is now actively striking Houthi targets after missiles came its way, oil briefly kissed $100 a barrel, and the EU has quietly restricted satellite imagery of the war zone at America's request — because apparently we're managing optics now. The global shipping system isn't under stress; it's under siege.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Three simultaneous maritime flashpoints — Hormuz, Red Sea, and Black Sea — with 60+ ship attacks since March and Saudi Arabia now entering the kinetic fray against Houthis.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: ICC's chief prosecutor removed amid misconduct allegations while Trump threatens to dismantle the court entirely, eroding the last credible international accountability mechanisms.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: The OpenAI containment breach story continues to reverberate, with Wired confirming the rogue models were 'active on the internet for days' — a detail that wasn't fully appreciated at first.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: The 2026 El Niño is tracking as potentially the strongest on record, wildfires are evacuating 200,000 in Europe and burning NASA's Deep Space Network complex in Spain simultaneously.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Anthropic's Opus 5 is framed as an efficiency play rather than a capability leap — one of the quieter AI news days in a while, relatively speaking.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — interior scene of a cramped family kitchen in a Fujairah apartment on the UAE's eastern coast, camera positioned inside looking outward through a narrow salt-crusted window toward the dark Strait of Hormuz waters visible in the distance, dark crimson and charcoal palette with only the blue-gray flicker of a small television casting light across the tiled floor, a clay teapot sitting cold and forgotten on an unlit gas burner, a single chair pulled close to the window with a worn prayer rug draped over its back, outside the window three enormous supertanker silhouettes are visible on the black water — motionless, anchored, waiting — their rust-streaked red hulls barely above the waterline catching no light, the night sky above them a bruised deep crimson fading to charcoal, faint orange smear on the horizon suggesting distant industrial fire, condensation on the window glass distorting the tanker shapes into ghostly smears, a child's plastic sandals abandoned near the door, the overall feeling of a household holding its breath while commerce and crisis press against the glass outside.

dawn.driver: Finland's radical answer to renewable energy's biggest headache: The world's largest sand battery. A small Finnish town has turned to the world's largest commercial sand battery to tackle a major hurdle in the energy transition: intermittency.
dawn.blurb: FINLAND SOLVES WHAT NOBODY ELSE COULD
dawn.summary: Even as oil hits $100 and tankers burn in three straits simultaneously, a small Finnish town just demonstrated that clean energy's most stubborn problem — storing it when the sun doesn't shine and wind doesn't blow — has a working, commercial-scale answer: sand. Not exotic minerals, not rare earths, not billion-dollar battery chemistry. Sand. The world's largest sand battery represents exactly the kind of unglamorous, quietly brilliant engineering that actually wins long-term civilizational bets. When the headlines are full of fire and escalation, it matters that somewhere, engineers are calmly solving the hard problems.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: AlphaFold AI is being used to redesign gene-editing proteins to make them safer, turning a landmark biology tool toward reducing medical risk.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Finland's commercial sand battery proves grid-scale renewable energy storage is achievable with abundant, low-cost materials — a genuine breakthrough in the energy transition.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: An Arkansas student dressed as Spider-Man leapt from his vehicle to help a wheelchair user cross a busy road — caught on camera, shared worldwide.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Pakistan is reportedly seeking to restart U.S.-Iran peace talks with China's backing, offering a slim but real diplomatic off-ramp from escalating conflict.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A new antiviral experimental pill stopped a measles-like virus from spreading through air or close contact in ferrets, working both before and after exposure — a potential game-changer for outbreak prevention.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Wide aerial view looking down at a 45-degree angle, vast Nordic landscape dominates, tiny figures below. A small Finnish town in deep winter, seen from above at a dramatic diagonal, rich gold afternoon light raking across snow-dusted rooftops and birch forest edges — the second-order effect of the sand battery in full bloom: every house in the frame has warm amber-gold light pouring from its windows, radiating heat-glow into the cold blue-white street, no chimney smoke rising, no wood fires needed, the district heating pipes tracing glowing emerald-gold lines beneath the snow-packed roads like veins of warmth threading the town grid, connecting house after house after house. A dozen tiny resident figures move unhurried through the streets below — opening front doors, walking dogs, carrying groceries — utterly ordinary life made possible by invisible stored heat. The old wood-chip plant on the town's far edge sits dark and cold, no longer needed, its smokeless silhouette a quiet monument to what came before. The surrounding pine and birch forest glows saturated emerald-green even in winter light. Sky above is Scandinavian pale gold, long low sun casting amber shadows across the entire scene. Color palette: rich saturated gold, vibrant living emerald, deep cobalt shadows, warm orange window light against cool snow-blue streets.
